Catacombs

The Catacombs are the first Dungeon in SkyBlock. It can be accessed through speaking to Mort in the  Catacombs Entrance or  Dungeon Hub.

Players are, by default, required to be in a party of 2-5 players in order to join the Catacombs. Ⓑ Bingo profiles are exempt from the normal party requirement. Giving Mort a  Saul's Recommendation from Adventurer Saul also allows players to enter the Catacombs on their own. You can set up your own party and invite your friends to join, or you can set up a party through the Party Finder, where you can select different options and requirements for people to join your party.

Overview

[edit | edit source]
  • The Catacombs are a series of floors, each with interconnecting rooms filled with mobs, secrets, traps, and puzzles.
  • The main goal of a run is to progress through the floor, defeat The Watcher, and then defeat the BOSS.
  • After killing all mobs in a room that have a ✯ star in their nametag, the room is marked as cleared and will drop:
    • a  Blessing and/or a  Superboom TNT;
    • a  Wither Key, which unlocks more sections of the floor. The  Blood Key is dropped when killing all ✯ mobs in the last room before the Blood Room and will unlock said room, where The Watcher summons Undeads that must be killed in order to progress to the BOSS room.

Rules

[edit | edit source]

While in the Catacombs, several mechanics are changed or disabled:

  • Potion effects from outside the Catacombs are paused while inside.
  • Only one potion may be consumed or splashed per run, with the exception of  Stamina,  Healing, and  Mana Potions.  God Potions cannot be consumed.
    • Players can receive effects from multiple potions if they are splashed or consumed simultaneously.
  • Players may not access the Auction House, Bazaar, Hex, or an Anvil, even while under the effect of a  Booster Cookie.
  • Players may not warp to private islands.
  • Players may not ride on mounts, like the  Armadillo or  Rock Pet.
  • Every hit on an enemy restores 5 + 1% of the player's maximum  Mana. This applies to melee attacks, bow hits, and the Mage Staff passive of the Mage class.
    • This does not apply to item abilities, such as Guided Bat from the  Spirit Sceptre, or class abilities, such as Explosive Shot.
  • All  Speed above 100  Speed is multiplied by 0.67.
  • Arrows deal reduced knockback and do not respect invincibility frames.
  •  Damage against bosses is reduced above certain thresholds, depending on the boss.
  • Dragon Tracer is explicitly disabled, healing from Vampirism is reduced by 10x, and slowness from Venomous is greatly reduced.
  • The Purse is not displayed, and bonuses from items that scale with coins in the Purse do not work.
  • All purchases from Dungeon Reward Chests or NPCs take coins directly from your Bank.

Classes

[edit | edit source]
Main article: Classes

Players can choose one of five Classes: Berserk, Archer, Mage, Tank, and Healer. Each class serves a different purpose and has their own abilities, class passives, and ghost abilities. They are more effective if only one of each are present in a party, although multiple players can choose the same class if they wish.

  • Berserks prioritize dealing as much melee  Damage as possible.
  • Archers prioritize dealing as much ranged  Damage with a bow as possible.
  • Mages prioritize using their item abilities to deal as much magic damage as possible.
    • A sub-sect of Mage, known as Left-Click Mage, uses their Mage Staff passive to deal high amounts of melee  Damage.
  • Tanks prioritize staying near their teammates and diverting as much  Damage as possible to themselves.
  • Healers prioritize providing healing and support to their teammates and themselves.

Ghosts

[edit | edit source]
Main article: Ghosts

When a player loses all their  Health in the Catacombs, they do not die traditionally. Instead, they turn into a Ghost and function as a spectator with unique abilities and limited access to the SkyBlock Menu.

Dying does not remove coins held in the Purse or degrade the  Piggy Bank, regardless of whether a  Booster Cookie is active. Ghosts can be revived during the run. If a player leaves a Catacombs run and rejoins it, they can return as a Ghost and be revived.

Ghosts can only interact with the environment through their abilities: these abilities depend on their chosen Class, and are listed below.

Has a 20s cooldown.

Has a 20s cooldown.

Has a 20s cooldown.

Rooms and Exploration

[edit | edit source]

Generation

[edit | edit source]

A Catacombs floor consists of connected rooms. Special rooms generate in 1x1 spaces, while Standard Rooms can generate in 1x1, 1x2, 1x3, 1x4, 2x2, or L-shaped[a] spaces.

The path to the Blood Room is guarded by a series of Wither Doors and ends at the Blood Door. The Fairy Room always generates along this path. At least 2 Puzzle Rooms generate in a floor.

Dungeon Mobs spawn in Standard Rooms at predetermined locations, with some rooms also having predetermined mob types. Dungeon Secrets also appear in predetermined locations. Finding a Secret grants loot or a team-wide  Blessing and adds +1 to the Exploration Score[b].

Room Types

[edit | edit source]

There are several different rooms in the Catacombs, organized by color:

Room Description
Starter Room The Starter Room is the room where the Dungeon begins: players can ready up and change their class in this room before the run starts. Mort can be found here, and he gives players a  Dungeon Orb on lower floors.
Standard Room Each Dungeon run mostly consists of Standard Rooms. They contain a multitude of mobs and secrets: some mobs will have a yellow star next to their names, marking them as unique. When all unique mobs, or a miniboss, are killed, they will drop an item and mark the room as complete: two of these are guaranteed to be a  Wither Key, and one of these is guaranteed to be a  Blood Key.
Puzzle Room The Puzzle Room contains a Puzzle that must be completed for the room to be marked as completed. Some can be failed, and others cannot: they can be reset with an  Architect's First Draft.
Miniboss Room The Miniboss Room contains a random Miniboss: killing them will mark the room as complete. The miniboss can be a Angry Archaeologist, Lost Adventurer, King Midas, Shadow Assassin, or Frozen Adventurer.
Trap Room The Trap Room consists of several traps and obstacles that must be overcome. They contain several secrets that must be all completed in order to mark the room as complete. Trap Rooms can generate from Floor III through Floor VII, including their Master Mode counterparts.
Fairy Room The Fairy Room consists of a large tree in the middle, with several Fairies surrounding it that drop a  Revive Stone when killed. A healing pool can be found near the tree. Killing a Fairy here revives a dead player, and a dead player can also kill one to revive themselves.
Blood Room The Blood Room is the final room that must be completed before the boss room can be accessed. The Watcher will summon lots of Undead that must be all killed in order for the room to be marked as completed: on higher floors, they will receive modifiers and some will take the appearance of previous bosses, like Bonzo, Scarf, the Spirit Bear, or Sadan's Giants.

Magical Map

[edit | edit source]
Main article: Magical Map

The  Magical Map replaces the SkyBlock Menu while in the main section of a Catacombs floor and shows the layout of the floor, player locations, and room completion status. Entering the BOSS room restores the normal SkyBlock Menu.

The map uses the following indicators:

  • ? on a gray background: the room has not been explored.
  • Nothing: the room is uncleared.
  • ✘: the room has been failed.
  • ✔: the room has been cleared and at least 1 Secret remains undiscovered.
  • ✔: the room has been cleared and all of its Secrets have been discovered.

Pressing Right Click or Left Click while holding the map runs /sbmenu.

Exploration and Rewards

[edit | edit source]

Dungeon loot is obtained from Secrets, drops from Dungeon Mobs, and Dungeon Reward Chests.

Finishing a Run

[edit | edit source]

A Catacombs run ends when one of the following occurs:

  • The BOSS is defeated.
  • All players in the run have either died and become Ghosts or left the run.
  • 60 minutes pass without defeating the BOSS.

Players do not need to complete every room or defeat every mob to complete a run.

Dungeon Score

[edit | edit source]
Main article: Dungeon Score

Dungeon Score is a value comprised of four categories: Skill, or the number of deaths and puzzles failed in a run; Exploration, or the percentage of the floor completed and the number of secrets completed; Speed, or the time taken to complete a run; and Bonus, which varies depending on the floor and active modifiers, like Paul's EZPZ perk.

  • 0-99 Score grants a D.
  • 100-159 Score grants a C.
  • 160-229 Score grants a B.
  • 230-269.4 Score grants a A.
  • 270-299 Score grants a S.
  • ≥300 Score grants a S+.

For more in-depth calculations, see Dungeon Score.

Dungeon Reward Chests

[edit | edit source]
Main article: Dungeon Reward Chest
  • When a floor is successfully cleared, player(s) can spend Coins to unlock different tiers of Dungeon Reward Chests, with each tier increasing in price and quality of loot.
  • The total Score achieved at the end of a Dungeon run dictates which Dungeon Reward Chests are unlocked. Completion of the floor unlocks the Wood, Gold, and Diamond chests; an A unlocks the Emerald chest; an S unlocks the Obsidian chest, and an S+ unlocks the Bedrock chest while on Floor V or higher. While on The Catacombs - Floor VII, you unlock an additional chest per phase of the boss fight completed.[Confirm]
  • When obtaining an item classified as an RNG Drop, the following dialogue is displayed:
-----------------------------------
RNG DROP! <username> just found a <item>!
-----------------------------------

Dungeonizing and Essence

[edit | edit source]
Main article: Essence

Items used in the Catacombs can be either normal items or Dungeon items. Normal items do not have a DUNGEON tag in their item type, while Dungeon items do. Some normal items can be converted into Dungeon items using Essence, a process commonly called dungeonizing.

Essence is a currency used in the Catacombs that can be spent on upgrades at various NPCs, used to upgrade items, and convert items to Dungeon items.

Dungeon items generally receive increased stats while in the Catacombs. The stat boosts depend on your  Catacombs level, the number of Star Upgrades the item has, and the number of  Master Stars applied.

If a Slayer item is converted into a Dungeon item, it can be used inside the Catacombs without meeting its Slayer level requirement. Most Dungeon items still require a certain  Catacombs level. Gear dropped by mobs also uses the entry requirement of the floor it dropped on while inside that Dungeon instance. For example, a  Zombie Knight Chestplate dropped from  The Catacombs - Floor VII requires  Catacombs XIV (14) normally, but  Catacombs XXIV (24) while inside the Catacombs.

Standard Star Upgrades can be obtained on a variety of items that are not limited to being Catacombs-exclusive; however,  Master Stars can only be applied to Dungeon items.

Stat Bonuses

[edit | edit source]

The stat bonuses from your  Catacombs level and Star Upgrades are calculated separately and stack additively on top of the final state increase, only modifying the stats of the item itself.

While in the Catacombs, each Star Upgrade grants a +10% stat boost, adding up to a total stat boost of +50%; each Master Star grants a +5% stat boost on top of the initial increase, totaling to a +75% increase in stats across the board.

General's Medallion additionally grants a +1% stat boost per digit, up to +5%.

Example: Catacombs 27 [+255%] + 5 stars [+50%] + 2 Master Stars [+10%] + 1000 Secret Counter (4 Digits) [+4%] = +319%, while in Master Mode.

This boost multiplies eligible stats by (100% + 319%)×.

Some Stats are not boosted by every source, such as  Attack Speed,  Crit Chance, and  Ability Damage. These stats do not receive the  Catacombs Level stat boost, but can receive Stars,  Master Stars, and General's Medallion digits boosts.

Item Quality

[edit | edit source]

Dungeon items that drop from Dungeon Mobs and Minibosses will drop with different base stats depending on the floor it was dropped on and a randomly generated number that dictates the stat increase percentage.

There are up to 10 possible 'tiers' of base stats, dependent on the floor the item was dropped on.

The bonus stats of dropped items can reach up to a +50% increase, which will result in its Rarity being upgraded.

Dungeoneering

[edit | edit source]
Main article: Dungeoneering

 Dungeoneering is a Skill that is leveled up through completing runs of the Catacombs. As players complete or fail Dungeon runs, they will increment  Catacombs XP and eventually upgrade their  Catacombs skill. Each level grants increased  Health and SkyBlock XP, and grants a multiplicative stat multiplier on Dungeon items of up to +485%.

Additionally, the first 5 completions each day award a 40% bonus to  Catacombs XP. Failed runs do not count towards this bonus.

Trivia

[edit | edit source]
  • The Professor was referred to as Oak on the Alpha Hypixel Network.[2][3]
    • This was a reference to Professor Oak from the Pokémon franchise. The reason behind the change is unknown.
  • The Catacombs was intended to have 10 floors, with Maxor in Floor 7, Goldor in Floor 8, Storm in Floor 9, and Necron in Floor 10. The other Wither Lords were initially scrapped with the release of The Catacombs - Floor VII, but were re-added with the release of Master Mode - Floor VII.
